memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then I will make my covenant between me and you and will greatly increase your numbers." Abram fell facedown, and God said to him... - Gen 17:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who does the work in this covenant. "I will make my covenant... I will greatly increase your numbers." God is the actor; Abram is the recipient. Back in chapter 16, Abram and Sarai tried to increase the family their own way through Hagar - and it brought only pain. Now God says, in effect, "Leave the multiplying to Me."

There is deep rest in this. God's promises do not depend on our clever schemes or frantic efforts. He takes responsibility for accomplishing what He has promised. Our part is not to manufacture the outcome but to trust the One who will bring it about.

And look at Abram's response: "Abram fell facedown." This is worship, humility, awe. He does not argue this time, does not propose a workaround. He falls on his face before the God who is Almighty. That is the only fitting posture before El Shaddai.

When we truly grasp that God is the One who accomplishes His purposes, it produces both rest and reverence - rest, because the outcome isn't ours to force; reverence, because we stand before a God of infinite power. Paul captured it: "he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion" (Phil 1:6). Stop straining to do God's work for Him. Fall facedown, worship, and trust Him to multiply.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you straining to accomplish what only God can do?
- When did you last simply fall facedown before God in worship?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Almighty God, You are the One who accomplishes Your purposes. Forgive my frantic striving. I fall before You in worship, resting in the truth that You will complete what You have begun.
Amen.
